name: mbrotZ
scope: Original full workload, fresh processes, default V8 tiering; setup excluded and final predicate included.

rust.name: mbrotZ
rust.setup_excluded: stdin read/parse; deriv also parses the complete supplied input and expected expression before its clock
rust.predicate_boundary: final original equality is included; report calls start.elapsed before formatting Result/CSV, leaving the final owned result alive

inspection.notes: Exact frozen WAT retains both descending loops, full row allocation, every pixel store, strict complex recurrence/threshold and matrix spill before[0][0] sampling. This supersedes a prior retained-work WAT of a later rebuild for this handoff only.

correctness.predicate: sampled scalar matrix[0][0] equals supplied5, as original
correctness.small: actual Node/Wasm and original Chez n=3,count2,result5; both reject changed expected999
correctness.complete_small_matrix: native module test checks all nine cells at n=3 plus complex-square components; not an actual-Wasm complete matrix dump

rust.timed: 1000 allocations of one75-row vector and75 complete row buffers, all5625 pixels per render in descending y then x order, escape recurrence, whole-matrix opacity and destruction, final sampled scalar equality
rust.representation: Complex uses two f64 fields and ordinary rectangular multiplication/addition; packed usize (32-bit in Wasm) row buffers hold integer escape counts. Fresh matrix and row allocation each iteration, deterministic zero initialization, immediate Vec destruction versus Scheme generic vectors/numbers and tracing GC. No boxed allocation per complex arithmetic operation.
rust.opacity: black_box n and entire completed Vec<Vec<usize>> before sampling[0][0]; extra opacity preserves all pixel work without adding full-result validation. Original test returns only[0][0], hide has different effects/allocation.
rust.source_semantics: Same rectangular complex product ac-bd, ad+bc, addition, pixel coordinates, initial z=z0, escape-test placement and limits; no manually substituted scalar square formula or formula-based result. Generic Scheme complex product by real step is represented as scaling both f64 components; the supported finite f64 canonical domain is explicit.
rust.optimization: The optimized exact frozen Wasm reuses repeated cross products and norm squares during z*z and unrolls the escape loop by two, preserving the f64 mul/add/sub evaluation results. No fused multiply-add or reassociation is introduced in the Rust source.
